topics.title: 13.1 How DNS Works
topics.summary: DNS organizes names hierarchically. Authoritative servers publish records for zones; recursive resolvers obtain answers on a client’s behalf and can cache them. The application’s local resolver path may add another cache or consult non-DNS sources before sending a network query.

blocks.text: DNS organizes names hierarchically. Authoritative servers publish records for zones; recursive resolvers obtain answers on a client’s behalf and can cache them. The application’s local resolver path may add another cache or consult non-DNS sources before sending a network query.

A cached answer remains subject to its time to live, or TTL. Changing an authoritative record does not instantly replace every cached copy. During a migration, account for both old and new destinations serving traffic. Lowering a TTL shortly before a change does not retroactively shorten already cached responses.

A DNS response also has a status. NXDOMAIN says the queried name does not exist according to the response; a timeout says no usable response arrived in time. These are different failure classes. Read the response rather than reducing every lookup problem to “DNS is down.” (R31)

Query one DNS record and inspect the response.
dig example.com A

blocks.text: The system’s name-service switch determines how functions such as host lookup consult sources. On many Linux systems, /etc/nsswitch.conf contains a hosts: line. getent hosts NAME and getent ahosts NAME are useful ways to exercise that configured path.

A local resolver service, such as systemd-resolved, may accept queries on a loopback stub address and forward them according to per-link settings. resolvectl status is useful when that service is present; it is not a universal command for every distribution setup. NetworkManager, DHCP, Netplan, and cloud tooling may own the upstream settings.
Inspect the owner of the configuration before editing it. A manual change that works until the next DHCP renewal is evidence that you modified generated state rather than the source of truth.
Linux example — 13.2
Compare NSS ordering with resolution.

grep '^hosts:' /etc/nsswitch.conf
getent hosts localhost

topics.summary: /etc/hosts provides local name-to-address mappings. A teaching entry such as 192.168.56.10 status.harbor.test can let admin1 reach the isolated server by name without operating a DNS server. It affects that machine, not the whole network.

blocks.text: /etc/hosts provides local name-to-address mappings. A teaching entry such as 192.168.56.10 status.harbor.test can let admin1 reach the isolated server by name without operating a DNS server. It affects that machine, not the whole network.

Back up the file and add only a clearly marked lab entry after verifying the address is assigned to web1. Avoid duplicate or conflicting names. Validate with getent, not dig, because a direct DNS query does not normally consult this file. Remove the teaching entry when the lab ends so it cannot silently override a later real resolver result.
Local overrides are useful for diagnosis but poor fleet-wide configuration. A forgotten override can make one administrator see a different server from every customer.
Linux example — 13.3
Inspect the local hosts file.

cat /etc/hosts
getent hosts localhost

blocks.text: /etc/resolv.conf traditionally lists resolver settings such as nameservers and search domains. On managed systems it may be a symlink to a generated file. Start with ls -l /etc/resolv.conf and inspect its contents to understand the path.

A nameserver of 127.0.0.53 commonly indicates a local systemd-resolved stub, not an external DNS server. Replacing it with a public resolver may bypass split DNS, VPN policy, or internal names. It can also be overwritten by the actual manager. Repair the per-link or manager configuration instead of fighting the generated file.

Search domains can expand short names into fully qualified queries. Use a fully qualified name when testing an exact target and account for whether a trailing dot intentionally prevents search-suffix expansion.
Linux example — 13.4
Inspect how resolv.conf is supplied.

ls -l /etc/resolv.conf
cat /etc/resolv.conf

topics.title: 13.5 Forward and Reverse Lookups
topics.summary: A forward lookup asks for records associated with a name. A reverse lookup asks for the name associated with an address, commonly through a PTR record. dig -x ADDRESS performs a reverse query.

concepts.definition: A forward lookup asks for records associated with a name. A reverse lookup asks for the name associated with an address, commonly through a PTR record. dig -x ADDRESS performs a reverse query.

cards.answer: A forward lookup asks for records associated with a name. A reverse lookup asks for the name associated with an address, commonly through a PTR record. dig -x ADDRESS performs a reverse query.

cards.question: What should you check after this section’s example?
cards.answer: Reverse records need separate provisioning and may not exist even when forward DNS works.

blocks.text: A forward lookup asks for records associated with a name. A reverse lookup asks for the name associated with an address, commonly through a PTR record. dig -x ADDRESS performs a reverse query.

Forward and reverse records are administered independently and can disagree. A PTR record is not cryptographic proof of identity. Some services use reverse names in logging or policy, so missing reverse configuration can still have operational consequences. Investigate the specific service rather than demanding matching reverse DNS for every private lab host.

For HarborStatus, the acceptance test is that the intended client resolves the service name to the approved address and reaches the correct certificate and content. Reverse lookup is a separate documented requirement when needed.
Linux example — 13.5
Compare forward and reverse lookup forms.

dig example.com A
dig -x 127.0.0.1

topics.title: 13.6 DNS Record Types
topics.summary: A records map to IPv4 addresses, AAAA records to IPv6 addresses, and CNAME records alias one name to another. MX records identify mail exchangers; TXT records carry text used by many protocols; NS records identify authoritative servers; SOA records describe zone authority and timing information. PTR records support reverse lookups.

Ask for the type relevant to the failure. A missing AAAA answer does not contradict a valid A answer. An old AAAA record can explain why some clients fail while IPv4-only tests pass. A CNAME creates a dependency on resolving its target; it does not copy the target’s address permanently.
Record a change’s owner, intended TTL, rollback destination, and propagation checks. DNS is infrastructure configuration, not an informal address notebook.

topics.title: 13.7 NTP and Time Synchronization
topics.summary: NTP synchronizes clocks using network time sources. A server needs an accurate clock for certificate validation, authentication protocols, scheduled actions, and meaningful log correlation. Time zones control presentation; they do not fix an incorrect system clock.

concepts.definition: NTP synchronizes clocks using network time sources. A server needs an accurate clock for certificate validation, authentication protocols, scheduled actions, and meaningful log correlation. Time zones control presentation; they do not fix an incorrect system clock.

cards.question: Explain 13.7 NTP and Time Synchronization. What does the source establish?
cards.answer: NTP synchronizes clocks using network time sources. A server needs an accurate clock for certificate validation, authentication protocols, scheduled actions, and meaningful log correlation. Time zones control presentation; they do not fix an incorrect system clock.

cards.question: What should you check after this section’s example?
cards.answer: Correct wall-clock display alone does not demonstrate synchronization with an approved source.

blocks.text: NTP synchronizes clocks using network time sources. A server needs an accurate clock for certificate validation, authentication protocols, scheduled actions, and meaningful log correlation. Time zones control presentation; they do not fix an incorrect system clock.

Clock changes also have application consequences. A sudden wall-clock step can affect logs and software that incorrectly assumes wall time only moves forward. Monotonic time is designed for measuring elapsed intervals, but not every application uses it correctly. Coordinate large corrections on databases and other sensitive services instead of forcing a step during an incident without review.
Treat time sources as dependencies with redundancy and an approved trust model. Merely seeing the time-service process running does not prove synchronization.
Linux example — 13.7
Read clock synchronization state.
timedatectl status

blocks.text: tracking reports the clock’s synchronization state and estimates; sources shows candidate sources and their selection status. Interpret them together with the installed documentation and the organization’s acceptable offset, rather than treating any reachable source as sufficient. A teaching VM may be briefly unsynchronized after boot or isolated from its configured sources. First establish network access and valid configuration. Do not repeatedly run a manual clock-step command to hide an unreachable source. topics.title: 13.9 DHCP Concepts
topics.summary: DHCP is both an address service and a configuration-distribution mechanism. A reservation associates a predictable address with a client identity; a lease has an expiration and renewal process. Network changes can therefore arrive later than the initial connection.

concepts.definition: DHCP is both an address service and a configuration-distribution mechanism. A reservation associates a predictable address with a client identity; a lease has an expiration and renewal process. Network changes can therefore arrive later than the initial connection.

cards.question: Explain 13.9 DHCP Concepts. What does the source establish?
cards.answer: DHCP is both an address service and a configuration-distribution mechanism. A reservation associates a predictable address with a client identity; a lease has an expiration and renewal process. Network changes can therefore arrive later than the initial connection.

cards.question: What should you check after this section’s example?
cards.answer: Check lease options, address, gateway, and DNS; a lease does not prove application reachability.

blocks.text: DHCP is both an address service and a configuration-distribution mechanism. A reservation associates a predictable address with a client identity; a lease has an expiration and renewal process. Network changes can therefore arrive later than the initial connection.

Troubleshoot lease acquisition separately from name resolution and routing. A machine can receive an address but receive the wrong DNS servers. Cloned VMs can also carry duplicated identity information that confuses reservations or lease behavior.

The lab uses the hypervisor’s controlled NAT DHCP service for outbound connectivity. Do not install and activate a second DHCP server on a physical or shared virtual network merely to learn the packet exchange. Use a fully isolated network and an explicit authorized scope.

Inspect DHCP-derived configuration on a NetworkManager client.
nmcli device show

topics.title: 13.10 Network Service Troubleshooting
topics.summary: Write down what the application asked, what the local resolver returned, what the configured recursive resolver returned, and what the authoritative data says when you are authorized to inspect it. This separates a stale local cache, wrong recursive answer, and wrong zone configuration.

blocks.text: Write down what the application asked, what the local resolver returned, what the configured recursive resolver returned, and what the authoritative data says when you are authorized to inspect it. This separates a stale local cache, wrong recursive answer, and wrong zone configuration.

For time failures, compare service state, selected source, reachability, offset, and recent clock changes. For DHCP failures, compare the intended network, client identity, lease details, and manager logs. Do not restart all three services at once: a simultaneous change can restore service while destroying the explanation of what failed.
A dependency check belongs in the service runbook. “The web server is healthy” should not silently assume that every client has a working resolver and a trustworthy clock.

labs.title: Separate a resolved name from endpoint health
labs.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
lab_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf -- "$lab_dir"' EXIT
cd -- "$lab_dir"
printf 'status.harbor.test 192.0.2.10\n' > dns.fixture
printf '192.0.2.10:443 unavailable\n' > endpoint.fixture
grep -q '192.0.2.10' dns.fixture
grep -q unavailable endpoint.fixture
printf 'name resolves; endpoint not established\n'
